{{convert|6|ft|9|in|m|abbr=on}} tall, he primarily played the [[small forward]] and [[power forward]] positions.[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=ESP&PlayerID=5247 Eurobasket.com Andy Panko basketball profile.] ==College career== After playing high school basketball at [[Bishop McDevitt High School (Harrisburg, Pennsylvania)|Bishop McDevitt]] in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]], Panko played [[college basketball]] at [[Lebanon Valley College]].{{cite news |author1=Frank Bodani |title=Small-college player has big-time talent |page=B1|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{cite news |author1=Jay Nagle |title=Small school, big dreams: NBA prospect blossoms |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98027458/small-school-big-dreams-nba-prospect-b/ |access-date=20 March 2022 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |pages=D1, D4|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{cite news |author1=Ira Kaufman |title=Seniors land auditions for NBA dream roles |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98027784/seniors-land-auditions-for-nba-dream-rol/ |access-date=20 March 2022 |work=[[The |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98027938/panko-looks-to-be-part-of-lvc-tradition/ |access-date=20 March 2022 |work=[[Lebanon Daily News|The Daily News]] |date=26 April 1995 |page=12|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} ==Professional career== Panko began his professional career in 1999 with the [[New Mexico Slam]] of the [[International Basketball League (1999–2001)|International Basketball League]]. He made his [[NBA]] debut with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2001, playing just one minute in a single game.{{cite news |author1=Glen Rosales |title=Panko allowed taste of good life in NBA |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98028287/panko-allowed-taste-of-good-life-in-nba/ |access-date=20 March 2022 |work=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |date=20 January 2001 |page=D3}} Panko played for the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) from 2002 to 2003. He won a [[CBA champion]]ship with the Wizards in 2002.{{cite web |title=2001-02 Dakota Wizards Statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/t-DLGDAK/y-2001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=March 12, 2025}} He was named the [[Continental Basketball Association MVP Award|CBA Most Valuable Player]] and earned All-CBA First Team honors in 2003.{{cite web |title=Andy Panko minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-pankoand001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 26, 2021}} He was named the [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|Spanish ACB League MVP]] in 2012, while playing with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|San Sebastián Gipuzkoa]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=8115 |title=ACB.com Andy Panko, MVP Orange 2011-12 . |access-date=2012-05-08 |language=es |archive-date=2017-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107055801/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=8115 |url-status=dead }} In July 2012, he signed with the [[Greek Basket League]] / [[EuroLeague]] club [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/98723/greens-sign-veteran-big-man-panko Greens sign veteran big man Panko] In December 2012, he was traded to [[Unicaja Malaga]] for [[James Gist]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/97629/malaga-trade-james-gist-to-panathinaikos-for-andy-panko.html Malaga trade James Gist to Panathinaikos for Andy Panko] At the end of the season he left Unicaja.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/102610/unicaja-malaga-part-ways-with-andy-panko-and-marcus-williams.html Unicaja Malaga part ways with Andy Panko and Marcus Williams] On August 14, 2013, Panko signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] for the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|title=Fuenlabrada signs Andy Panko|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/61495/fuenlabrada-signs-andy-panko.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=15 August 2013}} On July 29, 2014, he agreed with Fuenlabrada to play one more season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/129459/andy-panko-returns-to-fuenlabrada.html Andy Panko returns to Fuenlabrada] On May 30, 2015, he signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2015 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/162489/andy-panko-signs-with-vaqueros-de-bayamon.html Andy Panko signs with Vaqueros de Bayamon] On July 17, 2015, Panko signed with French club [[SLUC Nancy Basket]] for the 2015–16 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/169122/andy-panko-reportedly-signing-with-sluc-nancy.html Andy Panko reportedly signing with SLUC Nancy] On May 11, 2016, he re-joined the Vaqueros de Bayamón for the rest of the [[2016 BSN season]].{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20160512212511/http://www.vaquerosahi.com/nueva/2016/05/cambios-de-refuerzos-a-granel-para-inicio-de-playoffs-del-bsn/ Cambios de refuerzos a granel para inicio de playoffs del BSN]}} {{in lang|es}} On September 12, 2016, Panko signed with Mexican club [[Fuerza Regia]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/211592/andy-panko-inks-with-fuerza-regia-monterrey.html Andy Panko inks with Fuerza Regia Monterrey] He helped his team to win the 2016–17 [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|LNBP]] championship.[http://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/news/485843/Fuerza-Regia-celebrate-LNBP-title Fuerza Regia celebrate LNBP title] On April 4, 2017, he signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of Venezuela for the rest of the 2017 [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|LPB]] season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/231062/andy-panko-signs-with-guaros-de-lara.html Andy Panko signs with Guaros de Lara] On July 27, 2017, he re-signed with Fuerza Regia for one more season.[http://www.beobasket.net/news/36563/andy-panko-extended-one-more-season-in-monterrey-mexico.html Andy Panko extended one more season in Monterrey Mexico!] ==EuroLeague statistics==
